notes: In Spain, 'el mercado' usually refers to a permanent indoor food market with stalls, whereas an open-air street market held once a week is called 'el mercadillo'.

senses.definition: A building or open place with stalls selling food and other goods.

draftBefore.emotion: bustling and lively, enjoying the sight of fresh produce and crowds
notes: While 'el mercado' can refer to the abstract concept of the economy or trade, it most often refers to the physical place where people go to buy groceries or household goods.
Do not confuse this with 'la tienda', which is typically a smaller, single store or shop.
